newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil makes plan for Gullfaks satellites.
newsitem.headline: Statoil makes plan for Gullfaks satellites.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said on Thursday it had drawn up a draft plan for the second phase development and operation of the Gullfaks satellites in the North Sea.
Statoil said the plans were made following the recent recommendation by Norway's Gas Supply Committee that the three fields should be candidates for delivering gas to continental Europe from 1999.
In addition to producing some gas through the phase I subsea installations tied back to Gullfaks A, the phase II plan sees two additional seabed templates linked by flow lines to Gullfaks C.

Statoil said a rich gas export line also will be laid to both the platforms and tied to the existing Statpipe gas trunkline, possibly near to the Veslefrikk development. Gas would be piped to the Kaarstoe terminal north of Stavanger.

"The phase II project has very good economics, particularly if we're allowed to develop early enough to be able to use our existing infrastructure and operations organisation," Olgart Skollevoll, head of the project, told Statoil's Status Weekly newsletter.
Phase II is expected to yield 54 billion cubic metres of gas from the Brent formation in Gullfaks South. Statoil said there also would be "substantial" liquids output in addition to the produced gas.
